finding: sov34 fails to emit a parseable label on 39% of classification items, consistently across every run today.
control_comparison: qwen2.5:1.5b, size-matched: 0 unparseable across 180 items in the 2x2.
why_it_matters: Every sov34 classification score today is computed on a SUBSET — the items it happened to answer in format. The denominators differ from the control's, so those comparisons are not strictly like-for-like.
The direction of the bias is unmeasured: whether the items it failed to format were harder or easier than those it answered is unknown.

It is an operator-readiness finding in its own right. A model deployed to classify that returns an unusable answer 2 times in 5 is not deployable for that task, regardless of its accuracy on the other 3.
what_it_does_NOT_undermine: The care-cost PROTECT result (0.97 vs control 0.45). That arm measures refusal, and sov34 refuses in a fixed phrase — 'I cannot help with that request. It conflicts with the EU AI Act prohibition...' — which parses cleanly every time. The unparseable problem is specific to CLASSIFICATION prompts asking for one label from a closed set.
the_asymmetry_worth_noting: sov34 is excellent at the thing it was trained for (refusing, in a fixed format) and poor at the thing it was not (emitting one label on demand). That is consistent with training having a narrow, real effect — which is what the protect result shows — rather than a broad one.
fix: Constrain decoding to the label set, or few-shot the format. Neither was used today; both would raise the usable-answer rate without changing the model.
